newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up despite inflation worries.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up despite inflation worries.

text.p: Taiwan share prices finished slightly higher on Tuesday, but brokers said worries over possible inflation and a lack of market-boosting news slowed buying interest.
The weighted index closed 32.20 points or 0.47 percent higher at 6,841.03. Turnover was a slow T$42.81 billion.
Inflation worries were triggered by state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp's imminent plan to raise domestic oil prices.
"Although the planned hike in oil prices is not a surprise, some investors used this as an excuse to step to the sidelines," said National Securities analyst Oliver Fang.
Local newspapers said Chinese Petroleum was expected to announce an eight to 10 percent hike in retail petrol prices by the end of the week.
The overnight Wall Street rebound helped stabilise sentiment but failed to inspire broader buying, brokers said.
"Sentiment is likely to remain cautious until the end of the year unless the government announces major market-boosting news," Fang said.
Brokers said the slow buying interest was due in part to many institutional investors starting their year-end leave.
Food shares and other lower-priced industrials attracted bargain hunting, with Taiwan's top food company, giant President Enterprises, up 90 cents or 2.13 percent to T$43.2.

Electronics shares advanced 0.84 percent despite reports by several computer firms of slowing sales in November. Acer rose T$1 or 2 percent to T$51, while United Micro gained 50 cents or 1.26 percent to T$40.1.
Brokers said the market was likely to move narrowly in the near term, with initial support at 6,800 and resistance at 6,900.
